checkpoints.description: App binary launches under tauri-driver and a WebDriver session attaches to its WebView
The WebView renders a <body> element
The WebView loads a document with a non-empty URL (the platform shell or the offline fallback)
The document exposes a non-empty title
The LLM picker lists on-device models first, then the provider's cloud models, in one list
A not-installed on-device model pulls via the download_model IPC and streams live progress events (real smollm:135m pull against the compiled binary)
Cancelling an in-flight pull returns promptly and the app keeps answering IPC (the no-freeze regression fix)
Clicking a different on-device model while one is downloading shows the 'already downloading' notice (one pull at a time)
A completed pull installs the on-device model (check_ollama_status lists it); the selection UI is covered by odm-06
The nav-bar on-device badge reflects the selected local model, cased as written

Busy default ports at launch degrade to allocated ones: the MCP bridge and the offline server each bind a free port (preferring 8000/3457) and every consumer follows — local chat still streams, the offline cache still serves
Downloading an on-device model with Local Models off turns Local Models on first, which sets up the Model Manager (with a one-time notice when it was never installed), then starts the pull
On a freshly launched app with Local Models already on, the first local chat reaches the MCP bridge — warmed up at launch, or started by the chat itself — with no 'turn Local Models off and on' error
checkpoints.note: Live test, not a stub: needs ollama-mcp-bridge installed on the e2e host (turning Local Models on once installs it); covered meanwhile by the post_local_chat_with and launch warm-up Rust tests in model_manager.rs

checkpoints.description: With Local Models on, quitting Ollama while the app stays open does not break local chat: the next message starts Ollama again and is answered, with no 'turn Local Models off and on' step
checkpoints.note: Needs a journey that stops Ollama under the running binary; covered meanwhile by the post_local_chat_with 503 Rust tests in model_manager.rs

checkpoints.description: A local reply that keeps streaming for longer than 5 minutes is not cut off: only 5 minutes of silence ends it
checkpoints.note: Needs a model slow enough to stream past 5 minutes; covered meanwhile by the streaming_chat_client Rust test in main.rs

checkpoints.description: check_opencode_status reports Code readiness (installed / version / config_ready / sandboxed / supported / sandbox_ready)
install_opencode downloads and installs the pinned opencode release binary (live)
The freshly installed binary is discoverable on the augmented PATH — status reports installed with a version instead of re-downloading forever
A chat with real work keeps its own workspace under the app-managed root; an untouched leftover (just .git) is recycled for the next chat instead of stranding one dir per launch
A chat keeps the same workspace across calls, persisted in workspaces.json
The folder picker repoints ONE chat at an arbitrary path and leaves other chats untouched
opencode_close / opencode_permission_respond on an unknown id are graceful no-ops
The app keeps answering IPC while opencode downloads and extracts (setup-freeze regression)
set_opencode_skills materialises a mentor’s Agent Skills as SKILL.md packages (frontmatter + text resources), with hostile slugs/filenames confined to the staging dir
A skills rewrite drops deselected skills, an empty sync clears the tree, and `skills: null` ends a sync without touching it
ensure_vibe_skills installs the shared iblai/vibe skill set into the app data dir (live tarball fetch, daily sha-gated)
A permission prompt in one chat does not block another chat's turn
The 5-session cap evicts the least-recently-used idle opencode process
The permission prompt renders in the chat that raised it
The Code pill spins in place of its icon while skills sync, and the popover shows the amber note when the sync fails
A Code turn invokes a synced skill through opencode’s native skill tool (permission card, then skill content in context)
New Chat in the sidebar evicts the previous chat’s opencode process while Code is on
A Code turn’s opencode process runs inside the OS sandbox (bwrap / sandbox-exec) — only the workspace and tool caches writable, ~/.ssh empty
A second New Chat in one app run gets its own fresh workspace, and a chat’s folder follows it from the ephemeral first-turn key to its real session id

Killing the opencode process mid-turn: the answer continues in the same bubble with no visible interruption (one silent respawn re-sends the prompt), and a second kill in the same turn surfaces ollama:error
The Code approval mode (manual/auto) round-trips through ~/.local/share/iblai/settings.json, survives a restart, and an unknown mode is refused rather than defaulting
A mentor keeps one workspace across chats while another mentor gets its own, and New Workspace mints a fresh folder without deleting the previous one
Approvals is one mode for every chat, saved on this machine: the Code popover and the composer both show the mode in force and a switch applies to running sessions
The Code popover offers New Workspace and a platform-named Open Folder button (Finder / Explorer / the probed Linux file manager)

A between-turn opencode death (crash, idle reap, LRU eviction) is invisible: the next turn session/loads the same conversation back, and when a load isn't possible the frontend's transcript is resent so the agent continues; a mid-turn death keeps the input busy — the Stop button stays Stop and no suggested prompts appear while the backend silently respawns
A managed opencode older than the pinned version is re-downloaded at boot; a user's own PATH copy is never replaced

A new web project walks the 3-step flow: the default-template question, then the local-preview question (dev server + browser open at http://localhost:3000 only on yes), then one deploy question per project (yes = deploy now and auto-redeploy on later changes, no = deploy only on request), and replies never name the hosting provider
Text the agent emits before a tool call lands in the thinking section, never the reply bubble; the visible reply is what follows the last tool call
check_code_agent_status answers for Codex and Claude Code (installed / supported / signed_in, null when the probe can't tell) and refuses an unknown backend

install_code_agent installs the pinned Node runtime and each agent's ACP adapter (live), streaming progress on model:installation-log with source code-agent; status then reports installed with node_version and adapter_version
code_agent_sign_in for Claude Code refuses with the run-claude-in-a-terminal guidance instead of opening a browser (the app reuses the CLI login)
checkpoints.deprecatedReason: The in-app sign-in (code_agent_sign_in) was removed: Codex signs in in the ChatGPT app and Claude Code in a terminal, and the popover's line, the toast and the turn error say so.

checkpoints.description: The Code popover's Agent choice (ibl.ai / Codex / Claude Code) routes turns through the model key (codex/default, claude/default), keeps the mentor-LLM and on-device writers off it, restores the platform model on switching back, and stays hidden on phones and on desktop builds without the agent commands

The popover shows the selected agent's one quiet status line: Install with live progress, the signed-out line saying where to sign in (Codex: the ChatGPT app; Claude Code: claude in a terminal) with Check Again, the account once signed in, and the reason where it can't run
A Codex sign-in made in the ChatGPT app is picked up by Check Again and the status then names the account
A turn on a signed-out agent raises one sign-in toast saying where to sign in (Codex: the ChatGPT app; Claude Code: claude in a terminal) and no generic chat error toast

A Code turn on Codex streams into the same bubble (reply, thinking, tool calls, permission card) with the ibl.ai guidance delivered as developer_instructions and Codex's own mode following the Approvals toggle (read-only for Ask Me, full access for Automatic)
A Code turn on Claude Code streams into the same bubble with the ibl.ai guidance appended via systemPrompt.append and the session pinned to Claude's default mode

On launch the desktop installs the managed Node and both agents' ACP adapters by itself in the background (a pin bump reaches every desktop on its next launch); the Code popover shows an installing agent with a spinner and refuses the choice until it is ready while ibl.ai keeps working, and a failed install shows its reason with Install to retry
list_code_agent_models answers each agent's models (id, name, description) with the agent's own default and the saved pick, or refuses naming install / sign-in; an unknown backend is refused

The top-left model picker opens the SDK's LLM Selection dialog (LLMProviderModal in its cloudOnly mode, the same dialog the cloud picker opens behind a provider card) while Code runs on Codex / Claude Code (in place of the mentor's LLM selector and the on-device badge), lists Default with the agent's own default and the agent's models as cards, saves the pick per machine, and shows a failed list on the button with a click to retry

A Code turn runs on the picked model: the handshake applies it with session/set_config_option right after the mode pin, a live session takes a new pick without a respawn, and a model the agent refuses fails the turn naming the picker

While a Code turn runs, the line under the reply says in plain words what the agent is doing right now (“Changing about/page.tsx…”, “Installing what the app needs…”) on opencode, Codex and Claude Code alike, never a raw tool name; it stands down while a permission card waits, and each new step restarts its 20-second reassurance clock

A Code turn's steps fold into one quiet “N steps” row that opens to one plain-words sentence per step with a done / didn't-go-through / stopped mark, files by their last two path segments and web pages by their site, with the exact command, file or address one click away; after Stop or a crash-respawn nothing keeps looking busy
The task list the agent keeps (Claude Code's and Codex's plan updates, opencode's todo tool) shows as the reply's checklist and ticks off as it works

A permission card leads with what Code wants to do in plain words above the exact command or file, with no tool-kind chip, from the request's tool call on desktop and from the permission name on a paired phone; a Browse prompt keeps its own description
A failed Code turn raises one toast, saying what went wrong in plain words (stopped unexpectedly, took too long, no model picked, couldn't start, signed out) instead of the raw agent error
The app keeps answering while a Code turn streams a chatty command: a build's output never reaches the chat as events, only a tool call's visible changes do

An Ask Me permission card's Switch to Automatic answers it, saves Automatic (the composer's approvals icon and the Code popover show it), clears every other waiting card, and no later request in that turn raises a card — on the desktop and on a paired phone; each new card plays a short chime
checkpoints.note: Needs an authenticated UI session and a tool-calling turn, like code-08/code-10; covered meanwhile by the SDK's code-permission-card 'Switch to Automatic' cases, the SdkChat Vitest 'switches to Automatic from a permission card the way the approvals button does', the use-approval-mode-choice Vitest cases and the Rust queue/switch tests

checkpoints.description: The Code popover stays inside the window: Radix opens it on the side with more room and caps it to that room, and only its body scrolls, so the Code switch at its top stays in view (on a short window, or with Phone Access on)
checkpoints.note: Needs an authenticated UI session, like code-24; covered meanwhile by the coding-mode-button Vitest 'keeps the Code switch in view and scrolls only what is below it'

checkpoints.description: In the mentor chat the approvals button sits first in the composer's right-hand group, before the microphone, voice call and send, only while Code is on; with Code off that group gains nothing, and in the canvas split each composer shows its own and switching Code off in either takes it out of both
checkpoints.note: Needs an authenticated UI session, like code-23; covered meanwhile by the SdkChat Vitest 'Code approvals' cases, the coding-mode-button Vitest offer cases and the SDK's chat-input-form 'host action controls (slots.composerActionControls)' cases

checkpoints.description: In the mentor chat at phone width (below 520px) the Code pill shows only its icon while off, keeps its name while it is the only tool on, folds to its icon and × when Canvas is also on, and shows its name and × while its popover is open
checkpoints.note: Needs an authenticated UI session at phone width, like code-50; covered meanwhile by the coding-mode-button Vitest 'CodingModeButton in the SDK composer’s tool row' cases and the SDK composer-tool-row tests

checkpoints.description: Tapping the Code pill while Code is off turns Code on, the way the popover's switch does (the first folder choice, the on-device model check, the bubblewrap check and a phone's pairing all apply; where the switch refuses, the tap only opens the popover), and opens the popover; while Code is on a tap only opens or closes it; the × on the pill shows whenever Code is on and turns it off without opening the popover, and with Code off and the popover open it only closes the popover — on the desktop and the iPhone app
checkpoints.note: Needs an authenticated UI session, like code-50; covered meanwhile by the coding-mode-button Vitest 'tapping the pill' cases (and its 'its x' cases), 'forces the same folder choice the first time a tap on the pill turns Code on', 'only opens the popover on a tap while no desktop is paired, and turns Code on from the next tap once one is' and 'enables, from the pill and from the switch, without the desktop folder-choice flow (no picker on a phone)'

checkpoints.description: A paired phone's Code runs inside the Mac's sandbox: it can change files only in its workspace folders
checkpoints.note: Needs a paired phone driving the Mac's Code, which tauri-driver cannot run; covered meanwhile by the Rust `the_phone_serve_runs_inside_the_code_sandbox`, `the_phone_serve_can_change_files_only_in_its_workspaces`, `the_phone_serve_is_confined_to_the_workspaces_root` and `phone_code_starts_its_serve_only_through_the_sandboxed_command` (remote_code.rs), `the_app_never_writes_through_a_link_in_a_config_home` and `a_link_in_the_workspaces_root_is_never_used_as_a_workspace` (opencode_acp.rs), and the opt-in live `the_sandboxed_phone_serve_answers_and_is_confined` (`cargo test sandboxed_phone_serve -- --ignored --nocapture`), which starts the real pinned opencode the way phone Code does and proves a write in the workspace lands while the home and a secret are refused

checkpoints.description: An approval mode saved to the user's profile carries over to a computer that has none saved (an Ask Me chosen on another computer stays Ask Me), never overrides a mode this computer has saved, and a pick in the Code controls is saved to the profile too
